title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality Characterization
description: Formalizes when equality holds in the Cauchy-Schwarz (and Hölder) inequality: equality in (∑ fᵢgᵢ)² = (∑ fᵢ²)(∑ gᵢ²) iff f and g are proportional. Proved via the Lagrange identity, with extensions to inner product spaces.

meta.historicalContext: The equality condition for Cauchy-Schwarz has been known since Cauchy (1821): equality holds iff the vectors are proportional. Lagrange's identity (1773) provides an elegant proof by expressing the CS deficit as a sum of squared cross-terms. For inner product spaces, the equality case is fundamental to projection theory and the Gram-Schmidt process.

sections.title: Lagrange Identity
sections.summary: Proves the Lagrange identity: the double sum of squared cross-terms (fᵢgⱼ - fⱼgᵢ)² equals twice the Cauchy-Schwarz deficit.

sections.title: Sum of Squares Zero Characterization
sections.summary: A sum of squares is zero iff each term is zero. Extended to double sums.

sections.title: Cauchy-Schwarz Equality Characterization
sections.summary: Full iff: equality in CS holds iff all cross-terms fᵢgⱼ - fⱼgᵢ vanish, giving proportionality.

sections.title: Inner Product Space Equality
sections.summary: Abstract characterization: ‖inner u v‖ = ‖u‖·‖v‖ iff u = c•v, using Mathlib's norm_inner_eq_norm_iff.

sections.title: Hölder and Cauchy-Schwarz for Finite Sums
sections.summary: Hölder's inequality for NNReal sums and Cauchy-Schwarz as an independent consequence of the Lagrange identity.

overview.summary: Characterizes when equality holds in Cauchy-Schwarz: (∑fᵢgᵢ)² = (∑fᵢ²)(∑gᵢ²) iff f and g are proportional (fᵢgⱼ = fⱼgᵢ for all i,j). The proof uses the Lagrange identity to express the CS deficit as a sum of squared cross-terms, reducing equality to the vanishing of all cross-terms.
overview.keyIdea: The Lagrange identity ∑ᵢ∑ⱼ(fᵢgⱼ-fⱼgᵢ)² = 2[(∑f²)(∑g²)-(∑fg)²] connects the CS deficit to cross-term structure. Since each (fᵢgⱼ-fⱼgᵢ)² ≥ 0, the sum vanishes iff every term vanishes, giving the proportionality condition.

conclusion.summary: We formalize the complete equality characterization for Cauchy-Schwarz in both finite-sum and inner product space settings. The Lagrange identity provides an elegant algebraic path to the proportionality condition, and Mathlib's norm_inner_eq_norm_iff gives the abstract version. All 10+ theorems are proved with zero sorries.
openQuestions: Can the equality case for general Hölder (p ≠ 2) be formalized using strict concavity of log?
Can the a.e. power proportionality condition for integral Hölder equality be formalized?
